Today (October 29, New Calendar) the Church remembers the Holy Martyr Anastasia the Roman.

She lived in Rome during the reigns of the Emperors Decius and Valerian. At an early age she left all to embrace a life of unceasing prayer, entering a small monastery in Rome directed by a nun named Sophia.

For her faith she was brought before the governor Probus. She boldly confessed Christ, refused to honor the idols, and died under torture. An angel led Sophia to retrieve her holy relics, which are now venerated at the monastery of Grigoriou on Mount Athos.

Her life reminds us that what we now call monasticism was present from the earliest days of the Church.
